assessment.security_status_cs: Situace v Rudém moři a okolí Jemenu zůstává kritická kvůli eskalaci pozemních bojů, útokům na ropné tankery v Hormuzském průlivu a rostoucímu napětí mezi Hútíji a vládními silami podporovanými koalicí. Přestože některé dopravní aliance plánují opatrný návrat k plavbě přes Suez, pokračující raketové útoky a přísné americké blokády íránských exportů drží riziko dodavatelských řetězců na maximu.
assessment.security_status_en: The situation in the Red Sea and around Yemen remains critical due to escalating ground combat, attacks on oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz, and rising tensions between the Houthis and coalition-backed government forces. Although some shipping alliances are planning a cautious return to Suez transits, ongoing missile strikes and strict US blockades on Iranian exports keep supply chain risks at a maximum.

recommendations.reason_cs: Přestože se někteří dopravci pokusit testovat trasu přes Suez, přetrvávající hrozba útoků v Rudém moři udržuje provozní rizika a náklady na pojištění velmi vysoko.
recommendations.reason_en: Although some carriers are attempting to test the Suez route, the persistent threat of attacks in the Red Sea keeps operational risks and insurance costs very high.

recommendations.sector_cs: Obranný průmysl (např. RTX, Lockheed Martin, BAE Systems)
recommendations.sector_en: Defense Industry (e.g. RTX, Lockheed Martin, BAE Systems)
recommendations.reason_cs: Intenzivní vojenské operace, balistické útoky a potřeba doplňování protivzdušné obrany v regionu nadále silně podporují poptávku po vojenském vybavení.
recommendations.reason_en: Intensive military operations, ballistic attacks, and the need to replenish air defense systems in the region continue to strongly support demand for military equipment.

recommendations.sector_cs: Ropa a Plyn (např. Shell, BP, Chevron)
recommendations.reason_cs: Omezené dodávky rafinovaných produktů, jako je nafta, spolu s útoky na tankery v Hormuzském průlivu a nulovým vývozem z Íránu tlačí ceny energií prudce vzhůru.
recommendations.reason_en: Constrained supplies of refined products like diesel, combined with tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz and zero Iranian exports, are driving energy prices sharply higher.

recommendations.sector_cs: Evropský Spotřební sektor & Autoprůmysl (např. Volvo, BMW)
recommendations.reason_cs: Rekordní ceny nafty a nestabilní logistické trasy zvyšují výrobní náklady a podkopávají spotřebitelskou důvěru v Evropě.
recommendations.reason_en: Record diesel prices and volatile logistics routes are increasing production costs and undermining consumer confidence across Europe.

recommendations.sector_cs: Pražská burza: ČEZ, Komerční banka, Erste Group
recommendations.sector_en: Prague Stock Exchange: ČEZ, Komerční banka, Erste Group
recommendations.reason_cs: Domácí tituly čelí globálnímu makroekonomickému tlaku a inflačním obavám z energetické krize, přičemž bankovní sektor vyčkává na další vývoj sazeb.
recommendations.reason_en: Domestic equities face global macroeconomic pressure and inflationary fears from the energy crisis, while the banking sector waits for further rate developments.

recommendations.sector_cs: Evropské blue-chips (např. Airbus, TotalEnergies, Allianz, Rheinmetall)
recommendations.sector_en: European blue-chips (e.g. Airbus, TotalEnergies, Allianz, Rheinmetall)
recommendations.reason_cs: Energetická krize a vysoké ceny paliv zatěžují širší evropský korporátní sektor, zatímco energetické a zbrojní firmy těží z válečného prostředí.
recommendations.reason_en: The energy crisis and high fuel prices weigh on the broader European corporate sector, while energy and defense firms benefit from the wartime environment.

assessment.forecast_cs: V následujících dnech lze očekávat další eskalaci bojů v Jemenu a zvýšené bezpečnostní opatření kolem strategických úžin, přičemž trhy s ropou zůstanou extrémně volatilní.
assessment.forecast_en: Over the coming days, further escalation of fighting in Yemen and heightened security measures around strategic straits are expected to continue, while oil markets remain extremely volatile.
assessment.forecast_review_cs: Předchozí předpověď o pokračujících vojenských operacích v Jemenu a testování alternativních tras byla zcela potvrzena novými zprávami o těžkých bojích a pokusech o návrat k suezské trase.
assessment.forecast_review_en: The previous forecast regarding ongoing military operations in Yemen and the testing of alternative routes was fully confirmed by new reports of heavy fighting and attempts to return to the Suez route.

Alternative ways being used to move fuel out of Gulf region, but flows of refined products such as diesel still constrained

Exports of crude from the strait of Hormuz have largely returned to levels seen before the outbreak of the Iran war, as oil producers and the shipping industry have found alternative ways of transporting crucial fuel out of the Middle East.

Pipeline exports and ship-to-ship transfers are among the methods being used, according to analysts tracking the situation, while the US military continues to escort some vessels. However, flows of refined products such as diesel remain constrained, pushing prices higher.

articles.title: Netanyahu's UAE visit highlights Arab leaders' dangerous gamble with Israel
articles.summary:
Netanyahu's UAE visit highlights Arab leaders' dangerous gamble with Israel

Submitted by Mohamad Elmasry on Thu, 10/01/2026 - 18:25
Deepening diplomatic and military ties amid the Gaza genocide risk compounding public anger over repression, corruption and economic hardship
A billboard in Tel Aviv, put up by an Israeli campaign group, depicts Arab leaders alongside Benjamin Netanyahu and Donald Trump under the slogan 'Now is the time for the Abraham Covenant', 26 June 2025 (Jack Guez/AFP)
On

As Israeli elections approach, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is under mounting pressure following media reports documenting his alleged failure to act on warnings about Hamas's attacks of 7 October 2023.

Haaretz started sparked a storm on 8 September when it reported that UAE President Mohammed bin Zayed, perhaps Netanyahu's closest Arab ally, had delivered an "explicit warning" to the Israeli prime minister about 10 days before the attack.

The Atlantic then reported that Egyptian officials had repeatedly alerted Israel to an impending Hamas assault, with Egypt's then intelligence chief, Abbas Kamel, flying to Tel Aviv days before 7 October to deliver a warning in person.

The New York Times reported on 25 September that Netanyahu did not disclose the warnings to Israel's security chiefs during a high-level security meeting on 1 October 2023.

Just weeks from the 27 October election, Netanyahu turned to his old friend in Abu Dhabi.

On Sunday, he flew to the UAE for what was supposed to be a secret meeting. Israeli media reported that the hour-long meeting took place at the airport and was followed by several hours of talks with officials from other Arab countries.

Neither side has disclosed a detailed account of the talks, but Israeli media reported a bombshell: Netanyahu had asked bin Zayed to deny the reports about the warning, and bin Zayed had declined, with the UAE unwilling to be drawn into Israeli politics before an election.

Key Arab governments continue to engage with Israel on a largely business-as-usual basis, even as Israel commits atrocities in Gaza, the West Bank, Lebanon, Syria and beyond

Netanyahu's office dismissed reports of the request as "fake news".

The following day, Netanyahu declared on X that "foreign and hostile states and actors, including Arab countries" were behind "false blood libels" aimed at toppling his government, despite his own reported appeal to the UAE president for help.

Meetings between top Israeli and Arab officials at a time of unprecedented Israeli aggression underscore a dynamic that has persisted for years: key Arab governments continue to engage with Israel on a largely business-as-usual basis, even as Israel commits atrocities in Gaza, the West Bank, Lebanon, Syria and beyond.

The expanded session in Abu Dhabi, which Israel's Kan broadcaster said included officials from countries without ties to Israel, reportedly focused on regional cooperation against Iran.

Kan noted that aircraft from Morocco, Libya and Qatar, whose capital Israel bombed only a year ago, landed in Abu Dhabi during Netanyahu's visit.

Arab governments nevertheless appear to believe that they can separate their relations with Israel from Israel's expansionist aggression and from Arab public opinion.

In other words, they would like to be left free to pursue normal diplomatic relations with Israel while occasionally condemning Israeli war crimes and organising aid deliveries to bereft Palestinians.

This is a dangerous game.

Business as usual

Netanyahu has used his dealings with Arab leaders to justify Israeli aggression.

Since the start of the Gaza genocide, he has sought to frame the war as one in line with broad Arab objectives of fighting terrorism, even suggesting that Arab leaders have told him privately that they agree with Israeli war policy.

In one meaningful way, then, Arab relations with Israel do more than simply undermine Palestinians: they actually enable Israeli aggression.

Israel's post-7 October genocide and expansionist aggression have not upended Israeli-Arab relations to the degree that some observers anticipated.

The UAE continues to expand its commercial and security ties with Israel: bilateral trade rose 11 percent to $3.2bn in 2024, and in May an Israeli-operated Iron Dome battery intercepted an Iranian missile over Emirati territory.

Egypt signed a $35bn natural gas supply deal with Israel in 2025, and Morocco and Israel announced on 16 September that they were upgrading their diplomatic relationship to full embassies and ambassadors.

The Abraham Accords countries, especially the UAE and Morocco, have maintained or deepened relations through Israel's destruction of Gaza.

Egypt and Jordan normalised relations with Israel decades before the accords were signed in 2020, and their continued ties reinforce the same point: normalisation has largely separated cooperation with Israel from its atrocities against Palestinians, Lebanese and others in the region.

There is even continued discussion, in both Israel and the United States, of expanding the accords to other Arab states.

US President Donald Trump and Netanyahu continue to set their sights on Saudi Arabia, with Trump declaring in July that a US-Saudi civil nuclear deal was "totally subject to" the kingdom joining the accords.

For its part, Saudi Arabia has repeatedly said that it will not accept a normalisation deal without the establishment of an independent, viable Palestinian state.

Importantly, though, Ynet and other Israeli outlets reported that Saudi Arabia and Jordan were among the countries represented at the "secret" meeting in Abu Dhabi.

A senior Saudi official flatly denied the claim, while Amman called the reports "false and baseless" and accused media close to Netanyahu of circulating them "for electoral purposes".

Fear of revolt

These relationships highlight a massive disconnect between Arab leaders and the Arab street. Recent polling suggests that Israel may be as disliked in the Arab world as it has ever been.

Arab Barometer's 2023 and 2024 polling found support for normalisation in single digits in most of the seven countries surveyed, and no more than 13 percent in any of them.

The 2025 Arab Opinion Index, meanwhile, found that 87 percent of respondents across 15 Arab countries opposed recognition of Israel. Only 6 percent said they would accept it, and half of that small minority made it conditional on a fully independent Palestinian state.

Majority of Arabs oppose normalisation with Israel, pan-Arab survey finds
Read More »

The juxtaposition between the polling data and Arab governments' relations with Israel is striking. Some Arab governments are preserving, and even expanding, relations with Israel even as their populations express rage at Israeli conduct.

It is impossible to separate Arab anger at Israel from frustrations over economic hardship, government repression and state corruption.

From the perspective of many Arabs, concerns over policy towards Israel overlap with broader concerns over government performance at home: the governments that repress their citizens and fail to deliver on economic promises are the same governments that engage diplomatically with Israel in ways that undermine Palestinians.

This mix is potentially combustible.

More than a decade and a half after the Arab Spring, regimes across the region continue to obsess over the possibility of mass revolt.

For the past several weeks in Egypt, government officials and prominent media personalities have warned against the harms of mass protest, often highlighting the economic cost of instability and invoking the 25 January 2011 uprising by name.

On 29 September, President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi himself told his prime minister, cabinet, governors and security chiefs that the 2011 uprising had "almost thrown" the state "into the unknown", and that the two years of economic contraction that followed had left the country needing "at least 10 to 15 years" to recover.

Elsewhere in the region, governments have announced economic initiatives or cracked down on dissent.

Public frustration can simmer under the surface for many years, and no one truly knows when anger might boil over

Amman has unveiled a raft of strategic economic projects to weather what Jordanian media call an "economic storm", while Bahrain targeted Shia critics in March during the war on Iran and Tunisia arrested journalists in September.

It is impossible to predict whether or when another Arab Spring might occur. Public frustration can simmer under the surface for many years, and no one truly knows when anger might boil over.

In late September, little more than a week after the embassy announcement, protests against normalisation erupted across Moroccan cities.

In Tangier, where the authorities had banned the demonstration, security forces moved quickly to disperse hundreds of protesters and detained more than a dozen.

Amid a good deal of uncertainty, one thing is sure: Arab governments continue to engage with Israel at their own risk.

articles.title: Record numbers going hungry in Yemen amid escalating conflict, WFP says
articles.summary:
Record numbers going hungry in Yemen amid escalating conflict, WFP says

Hunger in Yemen is accelerating, with a record number of people unable to meet their food needs as conflict intensifies in the country, the World Food Programme said on Friday.

A record number of people in government-controlled areas of the country where the WFP can access are no longer able to meet their food needs, with three out of four households skipping meals, according to Matthew Hollingworth, the WFP’s assistant executive director for programme operations.

The total population of government-held areas is estimated at around 10 million people.

“The effect of this latest flare-up of insecurity on the food security situation threatens to be absolutely devastating,” Hollingworth told reporters in Geneva via video link from Rome.

Reporting by Reuters

articles.title: At least 80 dead in fighting between Houthis and pro-government forces in last 24 hours
articles.summary:
At least 80 dead in fighting between Houthis and pro-government forces in last 24 hours

Fighting in southwestern Yemen between the Houthis and pro-government forces has left more than 80 people dead in the past 24 hours, sources from both sides told AFP on Friday.

At least 55 anti-government fighters were killed in Taiz governorate - many by airstrikes - according to Houthi military sources. On the government side, sources reported 26 military personnel killed.

Clashes are taking place on several fronts, both inland and in the highlands overlooking coastal areas recently seized by the Houthis.

articles.title: Morning update
articles.summary:
Morning update

Good morning Middle East Eye readers,

Here are the latest developments: 

  • US President Donald Trump indicated that Washington could request European countries to release diesel from their emergency stockpiles, amid the war on Iran's impact on global fuel supplies. "We may ask them to do that," Trump told reporters on Thursday. Meanwhile, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said European states should do so "immediately".

  • Yemen's armed forces spokesperson early on Friday said that air force warplanes carried out 20 precision strikes on Houthi targets over the past three hours in Taiz province. The spokesperson said the attacks - which targeted Houthi movements, reinforcements, gatherings, personnel, vehicles and military equipment - inflicted losses on the group. 

  • Trump threatened severe consequences if Iran failed to reach an agreement with Washington, saying that the confrontation with the Tehran will end "very soon". "Either they’ll do something very proper and smart, or they won’t be around very long," Trump said.

  • The commander of the Quds Force in the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), Esmail Qaani, said that the US is faced with a "humiliating situation" across the Middle East. Mohammad Reza Naqdi, a senior adviser to the commander of Iran’s Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), also suggested that the US withdrawal from Iraq indicates that Washington's power in the region is waning. 

  • An oil supertanker is in flames in the Strait of Hormuz after it was hit by a missile, Iran’s Fars news agency is reporting. The attack took place eight kilometres off the coast of Oman, Fars reported, without attributing a perpetrator to the attack.

articles.title: US arrests Energy Department employee under claims of backing Yemen’s Houthis
articles.summary:
US arrests Energy Department employee under claims of backing Yemen’s Houthis

The Justice Department has arrested a man under claims that he attempted to provide material support or resources to Yemen’s Houthis.

The 51 year-old, identified as Ashton Hamed Ellaboudy, is a US Energy Department employee. 

"As alleged, a US government employee travelled overseas and used his specialised expertise in an attempt to aid the Houthis, a designated Foreign Terrorist Organization backed by Iran," the assistant attorney general for national security, John A Eisenberg, said. 

Eisenberg claimed that Ellaboudy "acquired materials for the construction of explosive material and drones capable of delivering these explosives".

"These allegations are so deeply disturbing that they almost defy imagination," he added.

Ellaboudy is scheduled to appear before a federal judge on 2 October in Washington.

articles.title: No Iranian oil exports in September: Bessent
articles.summary:
No Iranian oil exports in September: Bessent

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has claimed in a post on X that “Iran loaded ZERO crude oil onto tankers in September”.

The US has blockaded Iranian ports since April in an attempt to thwart Iranian exports, the most profitable of which is oil sold principally to China. 

The blockade, which Bessent claimed is severing Tehran "economic lifeline", has deepened Iran's inflation crisis, but had also long been blighted by reports of ships passing through it in spite of US efforts to contain them. 

Iran loaded ZERO crude oil onto tankers in September. The Trump Administration is cutting off the Iranian regime’s most critical source of revenue.

archive.security_status_cs: V Jemenu a v oblasti Bab al-Mandab eskalují ozbrojené střety, když vládní jednotky a saúdská koalice podnikají rozsáhlé operace proti Houthiům. Útoky na energetickou infrastrukturu a lodní trasy nadále ohrožují globální energetickou bezpečností a vyvolávají diplomatické napětí s Íránem.
archive.security_status_en: Armed clashes are escalating in Yemen and the Bab al-Mandab Strait as government forces and the Saudi coalition launch large-scale operations against the Houthis. Attacks on energy infrastructure and shipping routes continue to threaten global energy security and provoke diplomatic tensions with Iran.

archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, continued military operations in Yemen and heightened G7 diplomatic activity toward Iran are expected, maintaining volatility in oil and maritime shipping markets.

archive.security_status_cs: Eskalace bojů v Jemenu a oblastí kolem úžiny Bab al-Mandab výrazně zvyšuje bezpečnostní rizika pro mezinárodní námořní dopravu a globální dodávky energie. Zapojení regionálních i západních mocností do obranných operací a rostoucí diplomatický tlak na Írán podtrhují nestabilitu v regionu Rudého moře.
archive.security_status_en: Escalating fighting in Yemen and around the Bab al-Mandab Strait significantly increases security risks for international maritime trade and global energy supplies. The involvement of regional and western powers in defensive operations and mounting diplomatic pressure on Iran underscore ongoing instability in the Red Sea region.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat pokračující boje v zámořském jemensko-rudomořském prostoru a další diplomatická jednání G7, což udrží zvýšenou nervozitu na trzích s energiemi.
archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, continued fighting in the Yemeni-Red Sea theater and further G7 diplomatic talks are expected, maintaining elevated nervousness in energy markets.

archive.security_status_cs: Konflikt v Jemenu a okolí Rudého moře se prudce vyhrotil, přičemž probíhají masivní vojenské operace včetně stovek úderů vládních sil proti Houthiům. Roste diplomatický tlak ze strany G7 a Velké Británie na Írán, zatímco Saúdská Arábie obnovuje spojenectví s UAE za účelem zajištění exportních koridorů.
archive.security_status_en: The conflict in Yemen and the Red Sea area has escalated sharply, with massive military operations including hundreds of government strikes against the Houthis. Diplomatic pressure from the G7 and the UK on Iran is mounting, while Saudi Arabia is renewing its alliance with the UAE to secure critical export corridors.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat další intenzivní boje v jemensko-rudomořském regionu a eskalaci diplomatických kroků G7 a Saúdské Arábie.
archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, further intense fighting in the Yemen-Red Sea region and escalating diplomatic moves by the G7 and Saudi Arabia are expected.

archive.security_status_cs: Eskalace konfliktů v Jemenu a útoky Houthiů na Saúdskou Arábii ohrožují klíčovou námořní trasu Bab al-Mandab a globální energetickou bezpečnost. Saúdská Arábie obnovuje spojenectví s UAE a podniká rozsáhlé vojenské operace, zatímco G7 a Velká Británie stupňují diplomatický tlak proti íránské podpoře povstalců.
archive.security_status_en: Escalating conflicts in Yemen and Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia threaten the critical Bab al-Mandab shipping lane and global energy security. Saudi Arabia is renewing its alliance with the UAE and launching extensive military operations, while the G7 and the UK step up diplomatic pressure against Iranian support for the rebels.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat pokračování vojenských operací v Jemenu, nárůst diplomatické aktivity mezi Saúdskou Arábií a UAE a zvýšenou volatilitu cen komodit.
archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, military operations in Yemen, increased diplomatic activity between Saudi Arabia and the UAE, and heightened commodity price volatility are expected to continue.

archive.security_status_cs: Situace v oblasti Rudého moře a úžiny Bab al-Mandab zůstává extrémně napjatá kvůli eskalaci bojů mezi Houthii a provládními silami v Jemenu. Omezená průplavnost klíčových námořních koridorů a přetrvávající hrozby pro globální energetickou infrastrukturu nadále drží trhy v pohotovosti.
archive.security_status_en: The security situation in the Red Sea and the Bab al-Mandab Strait remains extremely tense due to escalating fighting between the Houthis and pro-government forces in Yemen. Limited transit through key maritime corridors and ongoing threats to global energy infrastructure continue to keep markets on high alert.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat pokračování intenzivních bojů v Jemenu, nárůst tlaku na diplomatické řešení ze strany G7 a přetrvávající volatilitu cen ropy kvůli bezpečnostním rizikům v námořních koridorech.
archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, intensive fighting in Yemen, increased pressure for a diplomatic resolution from the G7, and persistent oil price volatility due to security risks in maritime corridors are expected to continue.

archive.security_status_cs: Situace v Rudém moři a oblasti Bab al-Mandab zůstává vysoce napjatá navzdory postupnému návratu části ropných toků a plánům kontejnerových aliancí na návrat k trasám přes Suez. Útoky neznámých projektilů na tankery v Hormuzském průlivu a eskalace pozemních bojů v Jemenu nicméně nadále udržují vysokou prémii za geopolitické riziko v klíčových námořních koridorech.
archive.security_status_en: The situation in the Red Sea and Bab al-Mandab region remains highly tense despite the gradual return of some oil flows and container alliances planning to resume Suez routes. However, attacks by unknown projectiles on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and escalating ground fighting in Yemen continue to sustain a high geopolitical risk premium in key maritime corridors.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat pokračování potyček v oblasti Rudého moře a Hormuzského průlivu, přičemž trhy budou nadále citlivě reagovat na jakékoliv zprávy o obnovení plného provozu přes Suez.
archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, skirmishes in the Red Sea and Strait of Hormuz are expected to continue, with markets remaining highly sensitive to any news regarding the full resumption of traffic through Suez.

archive.security_status_cs: Situace v Rudém moři a okolí zůstává kritická kvůli eskalaci bojů mezi Houthi a saúdsky podporovanými silami. Navíc dochází k přímým útokům na ropné tankery v Hormuzském průlivu a diplomatické roztržce mezi Etiopií a Eritreou.
archive.security_status_en: The situation in the Red Sea and surrounding regions remains critical due to escalating fighting between the Houthis and Saudi-backed forces. Furthermore, direct attacks on oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and a diplomatic rift between Ethiopia and Eritrea compound regional instability.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat pokračování vojenských operací v Jemenu a zvýšené napětí v Hormuzském průlivu, přičemž trhy budou nadále opatrně testovat alternativní námořní trasy.
archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, military operations in Yemen and heightened tensions in the Strait of Hormuz are expected to continue, while markets cautiously test alternative maritime routes.

archive.security_status_cs: Situace v Rudém moři a okolí Jemenu zůstává kritická kvůli eskalaci pozemních bojů, útokům na ropné tankery v Hormuzském průlivu a rostoucímu napětí mezi Hútíji a vládními silami podporovanými koalicí. Přestože některé dopravní aliance plánují opatrný návrat k plavbě přes Suez, pokračující raketové útoky a přísné americké blokády íránských exportů drží riziko dodavatelských řetězců na maximu.
archive.security_status_en: The situation in the Red Sea and around Yemen remains critical due to escalating ground combat, attacks on oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz, and rising tensions between the Houthis and coalition-backed government forces. Although some shipping alliances are planning a cautious return to Suez transits, ongoing missile strikes and strict US blockades on Iranian exports keep supply chain risks at a maximum.
archive.forecast_cs: V následujících dnech lze očekávat další eskalaci bojů v Jemenu a zvýšené bezpečnostní opatření kolem strategických úžin, přičemž trhy s ropou zůstanou extrémně volatilní.
archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, further escalation of fighting in Yemen and heightened security measures around strategic straits are expected to continue, while oil markets remain extremely volatile.
